question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.challenge: www-authenticate: Basic realm="project44 Security Realm", Bearer realm="project44 Security Realm": two schemes in one header, each with a realm and nothing else (no scope, no error, no resource_metadata)
decoded.body: JSON: httpStatusCode 401, errorMessage "Authorization failed.", one error from source "API Gateway" saying credentials could not be verified, and a supportReferenceId (a per-request id, replaced by a labelled placeholder in the transcript after the run)
decoded.token-endpoint: GET https://na12.api.project44.com/api/v4/oauth2/token answers 405 application/json, "Request method 'GET' is not supported", with no www-authenticate: the endpoint exists and takes another method, and a GET is not treated as an authentication failure
decoded.developer-portal: GET https://developers.project44.com/ answers 200 text/html to this run; the registry's link checker, run from this container at 12:07Z today, recorded HTTP 404 for the same URL. The two requests differ in method and user agent, and the difference is recorded, not explained
decoded.mcp: none: the entry lists no MCP server and mcp.project44.com had no address record on 2026-09-13, so no MCP request was made
decoded.artifact-redactions: two Cloudflare __cf_bm session cookies and two supportReferenceId values are replaced by labelled placeholders in the transcript after the run; nothing else was changed

finding: project44 publishes no MCP server, so this probe is REST only. With no credentials, GET api/v4/oauth2/client-applications on the na12 API host answers 401 with a www-authenticate header that offers two schemes, Basic and Bearer, each naming the same realm and nothing else: no scope, no error code, no metadata URL. The body is a gateway error with a per-request support reference. A GET on the oauth2/token endpoint answers 405, not 401, so the token endpoint is reachable and simply takes another method. The two-scheme challenge matches the vendor's own authentication guide, cited in the entry: Basic to manage client applications and mint tokens, Bearer everywhere else. Same 401 and same header as the entry's 2026-09-13 note. The developer portal answered 200 to this run and 404 to the registry's link checker run from this container eight minutes earlier; both are on the record and neither is explained here. Nothing here measures what a client-credentials token can read.

reproducibility.command: for u in https://na12.api.project44.com/api/v4/oauth2/client-applications https://na12.api.project44.com/api/v4/oauth2/token https://developers.project44.com/; do curl -sS -i -m 25 "$u" | head -c 4000; echo; done
